'''Dimitri V. Nanopoulos''' ({{IPAc-en|n|ə|ˈ|n|ɒ|p|ə|l|ɒ|s}}; {{langx|el|Δημήτρης Νανόπουλος}}; born 13 September 1948) is a Greek [[physicist]] residing in [[New York City|New York]]. He is one of the most regularly cited researchers in the world, cited more than 57,000 times across a number of separate branches of science.

==Biography==
Dimitri Nanopoulos was born and raised in [[Athens]]. His grandfather, Dimitris Nakas, was an [[Aromanians|Aromanian]] and an ardent [[Greek nationalism|Greek nationalist]] who had migrated at the beginning of the 20th century to [[New York City|New York]], but in March 1914 moved back to his native land in order to participate in the [[Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus|Greek struggle for northern Epirus]], and died in 1916; Nanopoulos' father was born nine months prior.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.tovima.gr/science/article/?aid=260576&h1 | title = Δημήτρης Νανόπουλος: Φως στη "σκοτεινή ενέργεια" | publisher = [[To Vima]] | language = el | date = 22 March 2009 | access-date = 6 February 2017}}</ref><ref name="Nanopoulos2015">{{Cite book|last=Nanopoulos|first=Demetrios|url=https://www.patakis.gr/images/files/22530/22530/assets/common/downloads/A.pdf|title=Στον τρίτο βράχο από τον Ήλιο – Μία ζωή, η επιστήμη κι άλλα παράλληλα σύμπαντα|publisher=Patakis Publishers|year=2015|isbn=9789601660158|pages=13–16|language=el|author-link=Dimitri Nanopoulos|access-date=2021-08-03|archive-date=2021-08-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803122533/https://www.patakis.gr/images/files/22530/22530/assets/common/downloads/A.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Βορειοηπειρώτης ο διάσημος Φυσικός Δημ. Νανόπουλος. Αυτός που διόρθωσε τη θεωρία του Αϊνστάιν! |url=https://www.neb.gr/node/834 |access-date=2022-08-09 |website=Νεολαία Βορειοηπειρωτών |language=el |quote=Ο εγγονός του Βλάχου της Αλβανίας Δημήτρη Νάκα διάβηκε πολλά σύνορα.}}</ref> His father's name was Vaios.<ref name="Nanopoulos2015" /> His mother, Vasiliki Korasidi, was born in [[Kifissia]] but descended from the Greek island of [[Kea (island)|Kea]].<ref name="Nanopoulos2015" /> Nanopoulos studied Physics at the [[University of Athens]] and he graduated in 1971, continuing his studies at the [[University of Sussex]] in England, where he obtained his Ph.D. in 1973 in High Energy Physics. He has been a Research Fellow at the European Organization for Nuclear Research ([[CERN]]) in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]] and for many years has been a staff member and Research Fellow at the [[École Normale Supérieure]], in [[Paris]], [[France]] and at [[Harvard University]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], United States. In 1989, he was elected Professor at the Department of Physics, at the [[NASA]]-supported [[Texas A&M University]], where since 1992 he has been a Distinguished Professor of Physics, and since 2002 holder of the Mitchell/Heep Chair in High Energy Physics; he is also a distinguished HARC fellow at the [[Houston Advanced Research Center]] in [[Houston]], [[Texas]]. In 1997 he was appointed regular member of the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]], and, in 2005, President of the Greek National Council for Research and Technology, Greek National Representative to the European Laboratory for Particle Physics, [[CERN]], and to the European Space Agency ([[ESA]]).

He has made several contributions to particle physics and cosmology,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ellis|first1=John|last2=Nanopoulos|first2=Dimitri|title=Particle physics and cosmology|journal=[[CERN Courier]]|date=July 1983|volume=23|issue=6|pages=211–216|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1730921}}</ref> and works in string unified theories, fundamentals of quantum theory, astroparticle physics and quantum-inspired models of brain function. He has written over 767 original papers, including 15 books. He has over 57,000 citations, placing him as the fourth most cited High Energy Physicist of all time, according to the 2001 and 2004 census. Since 1988 he has been fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], and since 1992 member of the [[Italian Physical Society]]. In 1996, he was made Commander of the [[Order of Honour (Greece)|Order of Honour]] of the Greek State. 
 
He is one of the principal developers of the [[flipped SU(5)]] model, first proposed by [[Stephen M. Barr]] in a paper published in 1982.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Barr | first=S.M. | title=A new symmetry breaking pattern for SO(10) and proton decay | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=112 | issue=3 | year=1982 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(82)90966-2 | pages=219–222| bibcode=1982PhLB..112..219B }}</ref> It was further described in a 1984 paper by Nanopoulos, J. P. Deredinger, and J.E Kim<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Derendinger | first1=J.-P. | last2=Kim | first2=Jihn E. | last3=Nanopoulos | first3=D.V. | title=Anti-Su(5) | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=139 | issue=3 | year=1984 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(84)91238-3 | pages=170–176| bibcode=1984PhLB..139..170D | url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/149877/files/198402321.pdf }}</ref> and a 1987 paper by Nanopoulos, [[Ignatios Antoniadis|I. Antoniadis]], [[John Ellis (physicist, born 1946)|John Ellis]], and [[John Hagelin]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Antoniadis | first1=I. | last2=Ellis | first2=J. | last3=Hagelin | first3=J.S. | last4=Nanopoulos | first4=D.V. | title=Supersymmetric flipped SU(5) revitalized | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=194 | issue=2 | year=1987 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(87)90533-8 | pages=231–235| bibcode=1987PhLB..194..231A | url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/178057 }}</ref><ref>Stenger, Victor J., ''Quantum Gods: Creation, Chaos and the Search for Cosmic Consciousness'', [[Prometheus Books]] (2009) {{ISBN|1-59102-713-6}} {{ISBN|978-1591027133}} p 61.</ref>

On 17 October 2006 he was awarded the Onassis International prize by the [[Alexander S. Onassis Foundation]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Faces and places: Nanopoulos receives 2006 Onassis prize|journal=CERN Courier|date=January 2007|volume=47|issue=1|pages=37–47|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734009}}</ref> On 28 September 2009, he was awarded the 2009 [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] from the Italian Physical Society in recognition of his pioneering work in the field of string theory.
